verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. (a) The auditor's cost is understated: the initialiser form in LabConstrictor_streamlit also writes `kind` (app_manifest.py:40, manifest_form.py:21, tests test_manifest_form.py:41 and test_app_manifest.py:24) and content/submit.md:20 documents it, so a no-alias rename touches the site, the initialiser and 6 manifests (3 repos plus the issue template). (b) A new data/tasks.yaml with site-written synonyms is a second vocabulary held by the site, which AGENTS.md allows only if it holds labels, not app descriptions. (c) The proposed filter labels would assert task words the authors never wrote; mapping VLab4Mic 'simulation' and NucleiSky 'registration' is author-chosen so that is fine, but tasks like 'restoration' or 'segmentation' with zero apps must NOT appear (the auditor already says so). (d) The claim that napari hub uses a controlled list is unverified and should not be cited anywhere.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Stage it. Step 1 (site only, S, do now, shared with AC-4): build every filter select from the values actually present among listed apps (drop the dead Segmentation/Game options, add counts). Step 2 (only if the lab agrees to touch the other repos): replace `kind` by a single required `task` enum of the tasks that real apps need plus a few obvious ones (tracking, registration, simulation, segmentation, analysis, experimental design), with the label map in code next to the existing KINDS dict (cards.py:7) instead of a new yaml file, and the same value shown on the card. Change the schema, the initialiser form and its two tests, content/submit.md, the 6 manifests and DESIGN.md/AGENTS.md in one coordinated cutover; do not merge the site until the app PRs land. Move 'training' and 'testing' out of the task axis (testing is already registry section: testing; the Demo is exempt). Do not infer a task from `categories`, and do not normalise 'experiment design' vs 'experimental design' in the site: fix the VLab4Mic manifest spelling in its own repo. Skip a separate synonyms file for now (see AC-2).

verdicts.misleading_risk: High if built as written. The host plugin's status (napari-labconstrictor labconstrictor-project.yaml:5 'Experimental') describes the plugin, not whether this particular app's tools appear in it. Turning it into 'Experimental in napari' or, worse, 'In napari' (for status Available) on every app that lists `napari` in hosts would state something the site has not verified per app, and the Playground README says its tools appear 'once those hosts are set up'. The status enum also has 'Install from GitHub' and 'Deprecated' (labconstrictor-project.schema.json:12), which the proposed two-way mapping ignores. Removing the whole 'Works in' select hides a legitimate napari/Fiji discriminator (3 apps) just to dodge a wording problem.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Fix the wording, not the filter. (1) One function in hosts.py/cards.py that gives the host phrase used by the card chip (cards.py:64-65), the header badge (cards.py:70-71) and the Details row (pages_apps.py:146-147, 170-173, which currently says only 'Works in' with pills), so the three can no longer disagree. (2) Wording: read the plugin's published status from projects.resolve for the host's `plugin` repo and show 'napari plugin: experimental' (status text as written, never reworded to a stronger claim); for any status other than Experimental or Available, show the status verbatim; if the plugin has no status, stop the build naming the host. Keep it phrased as the plugin's stage, e.g. 'Experimental napari plugin', so it never says the app is verified inside the host. (3) Relabel the filter 'Also runs in' (or keep 'Works in') and make it data-driven (drops the Notebook no-op and, today, nothing else; QuPath remains only because the Playground, a testing app, is not in the filter's apps if testing apps are excluded from option derivation). (4) Edit AGENTS.md:29 and DESIGN.md:32,49 in the same PR. Do not claim anything about whether tools work; that needs a maintainer run.
